answer: For an atlas service mapping every knoll and garden, allocate subsidized queries through a trust graph rooted in audited institutions. Give each root a fixed quota and each endorsement edge a capacity. Allocate all agents' queries together as flows that consume those shared capacities. A cluster of fake agents can endorse itself but cannot increase the capacity entering it. More access requires earning endorsements from independent roots or paying to compromise them. Security depends on honest roots and global accounting; counting endorsement paths separately would let aliases amplify trust.
